title: Use generic functions in a Graphical User Interface (GUI)-environment

lessons.title: Windows, menus and the desktop
lessons.html:
Things that work the same in most programs

Most programs in a GUI, like Word, Excel, email and the farm system, use the same basic controls. These are called generic functions. Once you learn them in one program, you can use them in others.

A window

Each open program shows in a window. At the top right are three buttons:

ButtonWhat it does
_ MinimiseHides the window to the taskbar
□ Maximise / RestoreMakes the window fill the screen, or smaller again
X CloseCloses the window or program

The bar at the top with the program name is the title bar. Drag it to move the window. Drag the edge of a window to make it bigger or smaller.

Taskbar

The taskbar at the bottom of the screen shows open programs. Click one to bring it to the front. You can also press Alt and Tab together to switch between windows.

Menus and ribbons

Programs have menus or a ribbon at the top with words like File, Home, Insert and View. Click a word to see the commands. The File menu usually has New, Open, Save, Save As, Print and Close.

Dialog boxes

Sometimes a box pops up to ask a question, like "Do you want to save changes?" Read it carefully before clicking Yes, No, OK or Cancel.

lessons.title: Open, save, print and edit
lessons.html:
Everyday commands

Open

File, then Open, find the file and double-click it. Or double-click the file in File Explorer.

Save and Save As

  • Save (Ctrl+S) – saves changes to the same file.
  • Save As – saves a new copy with a new name or in a new place. Use it the first time you save, or when you want to keep the old version.
  • Save often, especially when there is load shedding.

Print

  1. File, then Print, or press Ctrl+P.
  2. Choose the right printer.
  3. Choose how many copies and which pages.
  4. Look at the preview, then click Print.

Only print what you need, to save paper and ink.

Editing

CommandShortcutWhat it does
CutCtrl+XRemoves selected text so you can paste it elsewhere
CopyCtrl+CCopies selected text
PasteCtrl+VPuts cut or copied text where the cursor is
UndoCtrl+ZTakes back your last action
FindCtrl+FFinds a word in the document

Selecting

To select text, click at the start and drag to the end. Double-click a word to select it. Ctrl+A selects everything.

An example from the wool store

The supervisor asks you to update the bale list. You open the file "Bale register 2026-03" from the shared folder. You find the bale number with Ctrl+F, type in the new mass, and press Ctrl+S to save. Then the supervisor asks for a copy for the transport company. You use Save As to save a copy called "Bale list for transport 2026-03-15", so the main register is not changed. Finally you press Ctrl+P, check the preview shows only the pages you need, and print one copy.

lessons.title: Help, settings and good habits
lessons.html:
Getting help and working smart

Help

  • Many programs have a Help menu or a ? button. Press F1 for help in most programs.
  • Hover the mouse over a button and wait – a small label tells you what it does.
  • Ask your supervisor or IT person if you are stuck. Do not guess with important records.

Simple settings

  • Change zoom (Ctrl and the mouse wheel, or the zoom slider) to make text bigger on the screen. This does not change the printout.
  • Change the screen brightness or volume from the taskbar.
  • Do not change system settings that your office has set unless you are allowed.

When a program freezes

  1. Wait a little – it may be busy.
  2. If it stays frozen, press Ctrl+Alt+Delete and open Task Manager.
  3. Choose the program and click End task. Unsaved work may be lost.
  4. Tell your supervisor if it happens often.

Good habits

  • Save often and use clear names.
  • Close programs you are not using.
  • Read every message before clicking.
  • Lock the screen (Windows key + L) when you leave your desk.

Key points

  • Minimise, maximise and close buttons work the same in most windows.
  • Save (Ctrl+S) keeps changes; Save As makes a new copy.
  • Cut, copy, paste and undo use Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V and Ctrl+Z.
  • Use Help (F1) and tooltips when unsure.
  • If a program freezes, use Task Manager to end it, then report it.
